# Helping Your Midwife Find You

### *(Written by the Riverside midwife who gets lost the most. You have been warned.)*

---

## Hello from all of us

You've chosen to have your baby at home. That's lovely, and we're really looking forward to it.

When the big day comes, we want to walk through your door calm, smiling and ready. We don't want to be driving round your estate at 3am talking to the sat nav. This page is all about helping us get to you **fast**.

In the Philippines, where one of our midwives grew up, people say the midwife is like family. That's how we want you to feel about us. We're not coming as strangers with clipboards. We're coming as friends who happen to bring gas and air.

So please read this, laugh a bit, and then do the checklist at the end. Future you (and future us) will be very grateful.

---

## First things first: when does home birth cover start?

**Our home birth cover starts at 37 weeks.**

If labour starts **before 37 weeks**, we can't come to you at home. You will need to go to the hospital. Please call the maternity unit on: **[HOSPITAL MATERNITY NUMBER]**

We tell everyone this at the booking visit. Everyone forgets. That's normal. Your brain is busy growing a whole human. That's why it's written here in big letters. 😊

---

## How to call us when labour starts

When labour starts, **phone the Riverside Birth Line:**

### 📞 [RIVERSIDE BIRTH LINE NUMBER]

This line goes straight to whichever midwife is on call. Day or night, someone will answer.

**Please don't ring a midwife's personal mobile.** We know you've got to know us, and we love that! But the midwife you met at your visits might be asleep, on holiday, or at another birth. The birth line always reaches someone who can come.

**When you call, please tell us:**

1. Your name
2. Your full address, including the postcode
3. How many weeks pregnant you are
4. What's happening (contractions, waters, anything worrying you)
5. Anything that makes your house hard to find

**After the call**, send us your location on WhatsApp to the birth line phone. You can drop a pin or send your **what3words** address. (what3words is a free app that gives every 3-metre square in the world its own three words. It's very clever, and it has saved us more than once.)

**In an emergency, always call 999 first.**

---

## Why we get lost (real stories, names changed to protect the innocent)

We're not making these up. Honestly.

**The Mystery of Flat 14.** One of our midwives drove round a block of flats in Everton for 20 minutes looking for Flat 14. It turns out Flat 14 was nowhere near Flat 13. It was in a different building! In the end, the dad leaned out of the window waving a tea towel. It worked, but let's not make it a tradition.

👉 *If you live in flats, tell us which building, which entrance, which floor, and the door code if there is one.*

**Rosemary Cottage.** A house with no number, just a name, in a long street of terraced houses. The sat nav took us to the chippy. The chips smelled great, but there was no baby there.

👉 *If your house has a name and no number, please tell us the nearest house number, or something we can't miss, like "the green door next to number 22."*

**The Wrong House.** Once, a midwife walked into the wrong house because the door was open. A very nice old man gave her a Jammie Dodger anyway. Lovely man. Wrong house.

👉 *Please make sure your house number can be seen from the street, especially in the dark.*

**The Balloon Family.** And now a happy one! One family tied balloons to their gate like it was a birthday party. We found them straight away. Best idea ever. 🎈

👉 *Balloons, a ribbon, a sign in the window, anything bright works. Have it ready in your birth bag so someone can pop it outside when you call us.*

---

## Lights on, please!

In winter, at night, every street in Liverpool looks the same. Dark houses, dark doors, parked cars everywhere.

**Please switch your porch light or outside light on** as soon as you've called us. If you haven't got one, put a light on in the front room and open the curtains.

---

## Parking: we need space for two cars

**Two midwives come to every birth.** We usually come in separate cars, often at different times. So if you can, please keep **two parking spaces** free near your house.

Ask a neighbour if they can move their car, or put the bins out on the road to "save" a space (then move them when we arrive).

### Permit zones (Anfield, Kensington and other areas)

If you live in a permit parking zone, please sort out a **visitor permit** from Liverpool City Council before 37 weeks. Keep it ready by the front door so you can hand it to us, or leave it where we can find it.

We have had parking tickets while we were helping babies arrive. It's not the best "welcome to the world" present.

---

## We carry a LOT of stuff

We'll arrive with gas and air cylinders, a big heavy bag, and sometimes birthing pool kit too. By the time we get to your door, our arms are tired!

**Please help us by:**

- **Clearing the hallway and stairs.** Move shoes, washing baskets, school bags, and especially **Lego**. Nobody wants to step on Lego carrying a gas cylinder.
- **Leaving the front door easy to open**, or having someone ready to let us in.
- **Telling us about tricky stuff** like steep steps, a back entrance, or a gate that sticks.

If your birth partner wants a job, carrying bags in from the car is a great one.

---

## Pets: we love them, just not during the pushing

We are big animal fans. Truly. But during labour we need to move quickly and keep things clean and calm.

One of our midwives knows a Staffie called Pippin who loves her very, very much. He jumped up at her every single visit. She nearly dropped the Entonox (that's the gas and air). Pippin meant well.

**Please put dogs, cats and any other pets in another room** with the door shut before we arrive. Have someone ready to look after them if you can. They can meet the baby later. They'll have their whole lives together!

---

## A little note from us

None of this is about being told off. We know life is busy, and nobody's house is perfect. We've seen it all and we don't mind mess one bit.

These small things just help us get to you quickly and safely, so we can do the bit we love: helping you meet your baby.

We can't wait to meet you. See you soon (and hopefully we'll find you first time!) 💛

*The Riverside Community Midwives*

---
---

## ✂️ FRIDGE CHECKLIST: Ready for Your Midwife

*Cut this out and stick it on your fridge. Tick things off as you go!*

**Before 37 weeks:**

☐ Birth line number saved in my phone **and** my partner's phone: **[RIVERSIDE BIRTH LINE NUMBER]**

☐ Hospital number saved too, in case labour starts before 37 weeks: **[HOSPITAL MATERNITY NUMBER]**

☐ Visitor parking permit sorted (if I live in a permit zone)

☐ House number can be seen from the street

☐ I know my what3words address: ___________ / ___________ / ___________

☐ Balloons, ribbon or a sign ready to put outside

☐ Directions written down if my house is hard to find (flats, no number, back entrance)

**When labour starts:**

☐ Called the **Riverside Birth Line** (not a personal mobile!)

☐ Sent my location pin or what3words on WhatsApp to the birth line phone

☐ Porch light on / front room light on

☐ Balloons or sign outside

☐ Two parking spaces kept free if possible

☐ Permit left out ready

☐ Hallway and stairs cleared (no shoes, no washing, NO LEGO)

☐ Pets in another room with the door shut

☐ Someone ready to open the door and help carry bags

**Emergency? Call 999.**

---

*Just so you know:* I've left **[RIVERSIDE BIRTH LINE NUMBER]** and **[HOSPITAL MATERNITY NUMBER]** as placeholders, so drop the real numbers in. It's also worth asking Deb to check two lines before it goes out: the bit about calling the hospital before 37 weeks, and the bit about what to tell the birth line. That way they match exactly what your team says at booking. I also told the stories as "one of our midwives" so it works as a team handout. Change it to "I" if you'd like it more personal for the Facebook group.
